advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard `result["digest"]` and `ds.content_hash(state)` per item in `_finalize_claims` so a malformed result / hash failure disposes ONE item (as the pre-restructure loop did) instead of aborting the rest of the batch.
evidence: `if state is not None and ds.content_hash(state) != snap:` and `ds.emit(result["digest"], tid, state=state, model=cfg.model, repo_root=repo_root)` (src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:459,467) run without a per-item guard
Pre-restructure diff: `result = enrich(...)` then `ds.emit(result["digest"], ...)` were both inside `except Exception as exc: ... _record_item_failure(exc, tid, ...)`

enrich() guarantees the key today (`return {"digest": digest, ...}` at src/rebar/llm/enrich.py:206), but a custom `runner` result shape or a content_hash failure would raise and abort the remaining batch
advisory.finding: In `_finalize_claims`, `result["digest"]` and `ds.content_hash(state)` are evaluated OUTSIDE any per-item try/except; before the restructure the enrich result access + emit lived inside the loop's `except Exception` routed to `_record_item_failure`. An exception on either now propagates out of `_finalize_claims` and aborts finalization of every remaining claimed item in the batch (those claims recover only on lease expiry), a wider blast radius than the prior per-item isolation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the per-item finalize body (snapshot compare + digest access + emit + mark_done) in a try/except that calls `_record_item_failure` for that tid, so one bad item cannot abort finalization of the others.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit at least a WARNING (or a counter in the summary) when `_snapshot_hash` returns None so an item that silently skips stale-revalidation is distinguishable from one that checked-and-was-clean.
evidence: `except Exception: ... return None` (src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:352-355)
In `_finalize_claims`, `if snap is not None:` gates the entire revalidation block (src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:454) — a None snapshot skips the drift check entirely and proceeds to emit
Docstring admits it 'disables revalidation for this item, degrading to the pre-restructure emit-without-revalidation behaviour' with no counter/log to distinguish it from a clean check
advisory.finding: `_snapshot_hash` collapses every exception to `None`, which silently disables the finalize-phase stale-revalidation for that item (degrading to emit-without-revalidation). A snapshot that FAILED to compute at collect time is indistinguishable from 'content did not drift': the verification produces nothing both when it truly cannot revalidate and could equally mask a hash it never captured, so a genuinely stale digest can be written back with no signal.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] _finalize_claims must re-verify the drainer still holds a live claim (lease not expired) before ds.emit + mark_done, or the batch must abort finalize for any ticket whose lease has lapsed.
evidence: Shared mutable resource: the per-ticket queue claim/lease and the ticket's digest sidecar — 'correctness rests on the optimistic claim + lease, not on the drain lock' (docs/llm-framework.md new section)

Executor 2 spawn: detached drain child per store write — 'spawned per ordinary store write by maybe_drain' (enrich_drain.py:5-7); overlapping drains pinned by tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py _ReentrantRunner / test_concurrent_drains_make_zero_duplicate_llm_calls

Sibling accessor + guard: queue.claim treats an expired lease as superseded — 'A lease-expired prior claim is superseded' (queue.py:521) and contenders filter 'if now < data.get("lease_expires_ns", 0)' (queue.py:544); the earliest live contender wins (queue.py:548). This is the serialization discipline.

Unlocked twin / interleaving: WRITE by drainer A finalize `ds.emit(result["digest"], tid, state=state, ...)` then `_queue.mark_done(tid, ...)` (enrich_drain.py _finalize_claims) with NO lease re-check; concurrently drainer B, after A's lease expired mid-enrich, executes the same claim->enrich->emit->mark_done on the same tid.
READ that is missing: _finalize_claims reads only `ds.content_hash(state) != snap` (content revalidation) — it never reads/re-checks `reduce_ticket(tid).claimed` or lease ownership before emit.

Harm: duplicate LLM spend on one ticket and a double digest emit + double DONE — the precise outcome test_concurrent_drains_make_zero_duplicate_llm_calls asserts must not happen, defeated whenever a batch's enrich exceeds the lease.
advisory.finding: _finalize_claims re-validates the content-hash snapshot but never re-verifies that this drainer's claim lease is still live before ds.emit + mark_done. Because the enrich phase (LLM calls) now runs with no lock held, a batch whose enrichment outlasts the claim lease will have its tickets re-claimed and re-enriched by a second drainer; both drainers then finalize, causing duplicate LLM spend and a double digest emit / double DONE on the same ticket.
scenarios: A single ticket's enrich hits the Anthropic tenacity retry envelope and the batch's cumulative enrich time exceeds overlap_lease_ttl_min, expiring leases stamped at collect time; a second concurrent drainer re-claims and re-enriches those tickets.
Provider latency spike making one item exceed the _WORST_CASE_ITEM_S=40 assumption baked into _lease_bounded_batch.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _finalize_claims, before emit+mark_done, re-check reduce_ticket(tid, now=_now_ns()) confirms this drainer_id still holds a live-lease claim; if not, skip emit and treat as re-claimed by another drainer (do not mark_done).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the lease-bound guarantee real: either re-verify lease ownership at finalize (Finding 1) or renew/extend leases as enrich progresses, since _lease_bounded_batch's per-item-average clamp does not bound worst-case elapsed time.
evidence: Clamp: 'lease_bound = max(1, (cfg.overlap_lease_ttl_min * 60) // _WORST_CASE_ITEM_S)' with _WORST_CASE_ITEM_S = 40 (enrich_drain.py _lease_bounded_batch, _WORST_CASE_ITEM_S)
Leases are stamped at claim time in collect: queue.claim sets 'lease = now + int(lease_ttl_min * _NS_PER_MIN)' (queue.py:526) using the collect-phase `now`.
Items are enriched serially in _enrich_claims ('for tid, snap in items:') so the last item's lease has aged by ~sum(item durations) at finalize.
Docstring asserts 'a run can never outlive its claims' (config.py comment / drain docstring) — the clamp does not actually guarantee this under a single slow item.
advisory.finding: _lease_bounded_batch bounds the batch by lease_ttl_s // _WORST_CASE_ITEM_S (40s) as an average-per-item budget, but all claims in a batch have leases stamped at (near) the same collect instant while items are enriched serially; the last item's finalize occurs after the sum of all preceding item times. A single item exceeding the 40s worst-case assumption expires the batch's leases before finalize, opening the lease-expiry re-claim window in Finding 1.
scenarios: One item in a 22-item batch takes several minutes (hung/retrying provider) while the other items also consume time, pushing total elapsed past the 15-minute lease before the final items are finalized.

This path silently changes the safety posture (a mid-enrichment edit would NOT be caught), yet the added tests only exercise the snap-present path (test_stale_writeback_is_skipped_and_reenqueued) and the drifted-hash path.
